Welcome.Title: StoryFlow - Dungeons LAB
Welcome.Intro: Thanks for installing StoryFlow! The whole Dungeons LAB crew hangs out on Discord.
Welcome.Help: Getting started or stuck? Ask - we answer.
Welcome.Request: Missing a node or a feature? Request it.
Welcome.Bug: Found a bug? Report it and we'll fix it.

Guide.Title: StoryFlow Tour

Invite.Heading: Shall I walk you through StoryFlow?
Invite.Body: A short tour shows how to run a story: build a scene, set the party a goal, hand out rewards. We highlight the right elements right inside Foundry, and nothing in your world changes.

Page1.Title: I'll walk you through StoryFlow
Page1.Body: This is the module's tour mode. While it is open, nothing in your world changes. I only show where things live and explain why you and the party need them.
Page1.Flavor: «Candles lit, map unrolled. Let's start small.»

Page2.Title: My name is LOBIK II
Page2.Body: I'm the Dungeons LAB mascot and your guide. The Second of my name, because the first LOBIK had an argument with a rock, and the rock won. I pop up over the window when something needs explaining and vanish once you've got it.
Page2.Flavor: «A small dragon with a large archive of notes.»

Page3.Title: One action per step
Page3.Body: Each step highlights a real element of the interface and waits for you to act. Do it, and the step is marked done. The current goal always sits in the tracker in the top-left corner.
Page3.Flavor: «Barovia forgives no haste, but hates waiting too.»

Page4.Title: You lead, I prompt
Page4.Body: «Next» moves on, «Back» returns. You can stop the tour at any moment: progress is saved and we resume from the same place next session.
Page4.Flavor: «When you're ready, knock on the shield in the sidebar.»

Finished.Title: Tour complete
Finished.Body: That's the basics. Restart the tour any time from the module settings.

Guide.RestartHint: Reopens the tour invitation window on this client.

Cheer.C3: Did you know my creators can build whole worlds? I can see you're good at it too. Will you teach me?
Cheer.C4: You learn faster than a dragon hoards gold!
Cheer.C5: One more step and I'll start taking notes from you.
Cheer.C6: My tail is wagging. That means you did well.
Cheer.C7: Careful, you're making this look easy.
Cheer.C8: LOBIK I once took on a rock and lost. You're doing much better.

Support.Title: Thank you!
Support.Heading: Support the creators
Support.Body: StoryFlow is built late at night by a small team of enthusiasts. If LOBIK II made your prep easier, a coffee on Ko-fi keeps him fed and the updates coming.

Calendar.Title: Calendar and events
Calendar.Blurb: World time, scheduled events and daily weather

WeatherShow.Title: A living calendar
WeatherShow.Body: The calendar generates weather for every day by itself, and the widget is animated: rain, fog and snow live right on it. Let me show you.
WeatherShow.Hint: Watch the show, then press Next

OpenCalendar.Title: Open the calendar
OpenCalendar.Body: The calendar drives world time for the whole table: seasons, weather and scheduled events. Its widget lives above the hotbar.

SeasonsGear.Title: Calendar settings
SeasonsGear.Body: Behind the gear live the calendar settings: seasons, temperatures and weather effects. Open it for a quick look.
SeasonsGear.Hint: Click the gear, take a look around, then press Next

CloseSeasons.Title: Close the settings
CloseSeasons.Body: That is where the climate is tuned. You can come back any time; for now, close the window and let us move on.

OpenEventDialog.Title: Add an event
OpenEventDialog.Body: An event is a note tied to a date. When world time reaches it, StoryFlow can fire a graph: a festival, a caravan, an assault.

SaveEvent.Title: Save the event
SaveEvent.Body: Give it a name, pick a kind (a plain notification or a full graph), and save. The calendar fires it when the moment comes.
SaveEvent.Hint: Fill the form and click the highlighted save button

CloseCalendar.Title: Close the calendar
CloseCalendar.Body: The event stays in the world. The widget keeps showing the current date and the nearest event.

JournalGraph.Title: Journal and graphs
JournalGraph.Blurb: Where StoryFlow graphs live and how to start one from a template

OpenJournalTab.Title: Open the Journal tab
OpenJournalTab.Body: StoryFlow graphs are journal pages: they live in your world's journal, not in module settings. That means folders, permissions and search all work as usual.
OpenJournalTab.Hint: Click the highlighted Journal tab in the sidebar

CreateJournal.Title: Create a journal entry
CreateJournal.Body: A journal entry is a container. One entry can hold several graphs, for example every scene of one chapter.
CreateJournal.Hint: Click «Create Journal Entry» and save it

OpenJournal.Title: Open the entry
OpenJournal.Body: The entry opens as a regular journal sheet. Pages are added from here.
OpenJournal.Hint: Open the journal entry you just created

CreatePage.Title: Add a StoryFlow Graph page
CreatePage.Body: Choose the «StoryFlow Graph» page type. That page holds the whole node graph: dialogue, choices, checks and world actions.
CreatePage.Hint: Add a page and pick the StoryFlow Graph type

OpenCanvas.Title: Open the graph editor
OpenCanvas.Body: The editor is a node canvas. Nodes are connected by pins: the story flows from an entry point along the links you draw.

UIAddNode.Title: The Add Node button
UIAddNode.Body: This button opens the node palette: dialogues, checks, rewards and the other story bricks. A new node lands on the canvas, ready to be wired by its pins.

UISearch.Title: Graph search
UISearch.Body: Search finds a node by name or text and brings the camera to it. In a big graph it is a lifesaver.

UIUndoRedo.Title: Undo and redo
UIUndoRedo.Body: Anything you do on the canvas can be undone and redone. Experiment freely: the graph can always roll back.

TemplatesIntro.Title: Ready-made templates
TemplatesIntro.Body: You don't have to build a story from scratch. StoryFlow ships ready-made template sets (dialogues, skill checks, shops, whole scenes) that land on the canvas as working graphs. Start from one, then bend it to your story.
TemplatesIntro.Flavor: «Why forge a sword when the armory is full?»

OpenTemplates.Title: Open the template library
OpenTemplates.Body: The library holds ready-made graphs: a dialogue, a shop, a skill check. A template is a fast start: paste it and rewrite the text.
OpenTemplates.Hint: Click the highlighted template library button

ApplyTemplate.Title: Try a template
ApplyTemplate.Body: Pick any template and insert it into the graph. The nodes land on the canvas; nothing is written to your world until you save.
ApplyTemplate.Hint: Insert any template into the graph

CloseTemplates.Title: Close the library
CloseTemplates.Body: The library is a tool, not part of the graph. Close it and the canvas is all yours.

NodesIntro.Title: A whole toolbox of nodes
NodesIntro.Body: Dialogue, choices, skill checks, rewards, traders, world actions: StoryFlow has dozens of node types, and every one is a building block of your story. You don't need to memorize them: the Node Guide explains each node with examples. Reading it is the best investment in your first story.
NodesIntro.Flavor: «Every node is a tooth in the dragon's jaw. Together, a bite.»

OpenNodeGuide.Title: Open the node guide
OpenNodeGuide.Body: The guide explains every node type: what its pins do, when to use it and which nodes pair with it. It is the reference to come back to.

CloseGraphWindows.Title: Tidy up the desk
CloseGraphWindows.Body: The graph is saved on its journal page. Close the graph editor and the node guide, and head back to the journal: a trader is waiting to be built there.

Trader.Title: Trader and shops
Trader.Blurb: Stock a shop and open it to the party, from the journal or mid-scene

Intro.Title: Meet the Trader
Intro.Body: A trader is a shop your players buy from and sell to. It lives on a journal page: open it straight from the journal, or drop a Trader node into a StoryFlow graph and the shop opens mid-scene. You pick the wares, prices and stock; StoryFlow runs the till.
Intro.Flavor: «Every good adventure starts at a counter with a little bell.»

CreateTraderPage.Title: Create a trader page
CreateTraderPage.Body: A trader is a journal page of the «StoryFlow Trader» type. It sits in your world's journal next to graphs and quests, so folders, permissions and search all work as usual.
CreateTraderPage.Hint: Add a page and pick the StoryFlow Trader type

AddItems.Title: Stock the shelves
AddItems.Body: Empty shelves? No problem. LOBIK will fetch the goods himself and lay them out: every row gets a price and a stock count.
AddItems.Hint: Wait for the courier, or drag items in yourself
AddItems.Say: I will fetch some items so you can try buying and selling!

RestockDays.Title: Automatic restock
RestockDays.Body: The in-game-days field makes the shop restock itself: a bought item returns to the shelf after that many world days. Zero means it stays gone until you restock by hand.

Restock.Title: Restocking
Restock.Body: «Restock now» is the manual lever: it puts everything sold straight back on the shelf.

CloseTraderSheet.Title: Close the settings
CloseTraderSheet.Body: The stock is set. Close the trader settings sheet; the shop itself is opened from the page, not from here.

OpenTraderPage.Title: Open the trader page
OpenTraderPage.Body: The new trader page sits in the entry's page list, and it does not open by itself. Click it: the page holds the shop button the party will use.
OpenTraderPage.Hint: Click the highlighted trader page in the list

OpenShop.Title: Open the shop
OpenShop.Body: The «Open Shop» button shows exactly what a player sees: the storefront with search, categories and the ledger cart. My favorite moment, watch closely.

ShopBuyer.Title: Who is buying
ShopBuyer.Body: The GM picks in this list who the purchase belongs to. For players it is simpler: the shop binds to their character by itself.

ShopWallet.Title: The wallet
ShopWallet.Body: This shows the buyer's coins. The shop itself makes sure the gold is enough.

ShopCart.Title: The cart
ShopCart.Body: This button opens the cart: goods pile up in it and check out as one purchase.

ShopSell.Title: Selling
ShopSell.Body: The Sell tab works the other way around: players turn their loot into the trader's gold.

CloseShop.Title: Close the shop
CloseShop.Body: Wares and prices stay on the page. The shop reopens any time: from the same button, a map pin, or a Trader node in a graph.

QuestBoard.Title: Quest Board
QuestBoard.Blurb: A shared party quest log: quests, lore and dramatic reveals

Intro.Title: Meet the Quest Board
Intro.Body: The Quest Board is the party's shared quest log: quests and lore in one window. You write the entries, attach rewards and factions, and reveal each one when the party is ready. Players only ever see what you revealed.
Intro.Flavor: «A tavern notice board, minus the damp parchment and the rat cellars.»

OpenBoard.Title: Open the board
OpenBoard.Body: The launcher lives in the token scene controls, the scroll icon. One click opens the board for you; players have the same button on their side.
OpenBoard.Hint: Click the highlighted scroll tool in the scene controls

AddQuest.Title: Add a quest
AddQuest.Body: «New Quest» creates a quest page in the board's own journal. Status, objectives, category and description all edit right here in the detail pane.

Objectives.Title: Quest objectives
Objectives.Body: Objectives are the quest steps the party can see. The button below adds one; the eye hides it for later, the arrows reorder it, the checkbox marks it done.
Objectives.Hint: Click the highlighted button and add an objective

RewardsSetup.Title: The rewards
RewardsSetup.Body: The rewards section holds gold, experience, reputation and items. LOBIK will now drop an item in and set the gold himself.
RewardsSetup.Say: Let me toss in a reward: an item and some gold!

AnnounceQuest.Title: Announce the quest
AnnounceQuest.Body: The announce button does everything at once: reveals the quest to the party, drops a card into chat and pings every player.

GiveReward.Title: Hand out the rewards
GiveReward.Body: The reward button starts dividing the spoils. Players raise a hand on the items they want; when two want the same item, a die is rolled and the winner takes it. Gold and experience split themselves.

DistributeRewards.Title: Divide the spoils
DistributeRewards.Body: This window is the payout. Gold and experience split evenly with one click. Items go by hand: players raise a hand on what they want, and when two hands are up on the same item, the roll-off button lets the dice decide. Confirm hands everything out.
DistributeRewards.Hint: Try the buttons, then confirm (or cancel)

CloseLedger.Title: Close the payout
CloseLedger.Body: Rewards are on their way. Close this window; next we tidy up the board itself.

CloseBoard.Title: Close the board
CloseBoard.Body: Everything is saved in the world journal. Reopen the board any time from the same scene-control tool.

Extras.Title: Dungeon LAB Modules
Extras.GMOnly: Only the Game Master can change this world-wide setting.

Factions.Name: Factions & Reputation
Factions.Hint: Track faction standing and NPC affinity: the Factions tab on character sheets, the Faction Codex, and the reputation nodes. World-wide - GM only.
Factions.Description:
The Factions plugin turns loose alliances into something the game tracks for you. Every actor gains a Factions tab: where they stand with each faction, tier by tier, from Hated to Exalted, plus how individual NPCs feel about the party.
Authors get reputation nodes on the graph canvas - raise or lower standing as a reward, gate a door or a price on a tier, swing an NPC's mood after a choice - and a Faction Codex the party can browse. The Trader shop and Condition checks read the same standing, so a hard-won reputation actually changes what the world offers.
This is a world-wide switch, so only the Game Master can flip it. The sheet tab and codex hide the moment it's off; the reputation nodes and service update after the next world reload.
Factions.ReloadHint: Factions setting saved. Reload the world to apply the reputation nodes and service.

DlTheme.Name: Dungeons LAB theme
DlTheme.Hint: Skin the module's UI in the Dungeons LAB look - candlelight ember on Barovian stone. Applies to this panel, the GM Scene Dashboard and the Actors sidebar. Personal to your client.
DlTheme.Description:
By default the module wears Foundry's own clothes - whatever theme your world runs, its panels blend in. Switch this on and they put on the Dungeons LAB colours instead: deep Barovian stone, candlelight-ember accents, a warm glow on whatever you have selected, and a serif hand on the headings.
It re-skins the Dungeon LAB Modules panel, the GM Scene Dashboard and the Actors sidebar in one stroke - and touches nothing else on your screen. Purely your view; off until you want it, and reversible in a single click.

ActorTint.Name: Group & colour actors by type
ActorTint.Hint: Group the Actors sidebar into type sections and softly tint each row, with a distinct shade for player-owned characters. Personal to your client.
ActorTint.Description:
Picture the eve of a big session: your Actors tab has swollen into a grey avalanche of names - heroes, hirelings, that one war-galley, a bestiary's worth of goblins - all wearing the same drab colour, all jumbled together in the order you happened to import them.
Foundry gives every actor the same neutral row, so telling a player character from an NPC from a vehicle means reading each name one at a time. Add a few dozen monsters and the party's own heroes vanish into the crowd right when you need them.
Switch this on and the sidebar sorts itself into tidy type sections - Characters, NPCs, Vehicles, Groups - each row washed in a soft, readable colour so the type registers at a glance. And it isn't limited to the usual suspects: the type list is read live from your game, so every actor type your system or your modules add gets its own distinct, consistent colour instead of drowning in a nameless grey. Your players' own characters get a brighter shade and a little accent stripe, so the heroes always stand out from the horde. It works inside your folders too, and it's purely your view - nobody else's screen changes.

ItemTint.Name: Group & colour items by type
ItemTint.Hint: Group the Items sidebar into type sections and softly tint each row, with a distinct shade per item type. Personal to your client.
ItemTint.Description:
The Items tab has the same problem as the Actors one, only worse: weapons, spells, consumables, features, loot and a dozen homebrew types, all poured into one long grey list in import order.
Foundry gives every item the same neutral row, so finding the one longsword among fifty scrolls means reading each name in turn. The bigger your compendium-fed world grows, the more the thing you want hides in the crowd.
Switch this on and the sidebar sorts itself into tidy type sections - Weapons, Spells, Consumables, Features and the rest - each row washed in a soft, readable colour so the type registers at a glance. The type list is read live from your game, so every item type your system or modules add gets its own distinct, consistent colour instead of drowning in a nameless grey. It works inside your folders too, and it's purely your view - nobody else's screen changes.

DragScroll.Name: Auto-scroll while dragging
DragScroll.Hint: Dragging a sidebar entry near the top or bottom edge scrolls the list, so you can reach a far-off folder. Works in every sidebar tab.
DragScroll.Description:
You know the move: the actor you want to file lives at the very bottom of a long list, so you grab it, aim for a folder near the top - and the sidebar just… sits there. The list won't budge while you're holding the drag, and there's no way to reach the destination without letting go and losing your place.
It's one of those small Foundry papercuts that costs you three fumbling attempts every time you tidy up.
With this on, holding a dragged entry near the top or bottom edge of any sidebar list gently scrolls it in that direction - faster the closer you hover to the edge - carrying your grip along until the target folder rolls into view. Actors, items, journals, scenes: every sidebar tab, always ready, no setting required.

MoveFolder.Name: Right-click → move to folder
MoveFolder.Hint: A right-click option on an actor or item that opens a picker to drop it straight into any folder - no dragging at all.
MoveFolder.Description:
Sometimes you don't want to drag at all. The folder is collapsed, or it's clear across a scrolled list, or you just have thirty actors (or items) to sort and dragging each one is death by a thousand clicks.
Foundry's only way to re-file a document is to physically haul it there - fine for one, a chore for many.
Right-click any actor or item and choose "Move to folder…" to open a tidy picker: pick the destination (or send it back to the root) and it's done, instantly, no aiming required. The dialog names the document you're moving and tints it with its type colour, so you always know exactly what's about to change homes - and only one window ever opens, no matter how many times you click.
