display.Summary: Shows a cinematic dialogue beat: speaker name, portrait, backdrop, and typewriter body text.
display.Usage: Set a speaker name and body text; optionally add a portrait and a backdrop image. Pacing controls: typewriter speed (cps), or auto-advance with a delay instead of waiting for a click. Voice-over and ambient audio can play with the beat. One input, one output - chain displays to build a scene.
display.Tip1: Leave the backdrop empty to keep the previous node's backdrop - scenes flow without flicker.
display.Tip2: Auto-advance with ~1500 ms reads like a film cut; keep click-to-advance for anything the players must actually read.
display.Tip3: The body is enriched HTML - @UUID links to actors and items work.

Pair.text: Text is the narrator's version of Display - no speaker, pure prose between beats.
Pair.choice: Follow a Display beat with a Choice to hand the scene to the players.
Pair.audio: Start a music bed just before a Display chain to score the scene.

choice.Summary: Presents options to the triggering player; each option is its own output pin and branch.
choice.Usage:
Write a prompt and add choices - each choice becomes a positional output pin (choice_0, choice_1, …). Only the triggering player can select; everyone else sees the options and can cast an advisory vote. Options can be gated (item, class…) and a timeout can auto-pick a path via the timeout pin.

[!info] A gated choice fails OPEN for a solo GM with no assigned character, staying visible rather than hiding from "nobody" - it only hides from a character that actually fails the gate.
choice.Tip1: Deleting a choice remaps the remaining pins - re-check your wiring after removing options.
choice.Tip2: A dead-end choice pin simply ends the run; wire every option somewhere, even if it is a shared Jump.
choice.Tip3: Use short labels - long options wrap and push the prompt off smaller screens.

Pair.display: Set the scene with a Display beat before asking the question.
Pair.check: Route a risky option into a Check so choosing it still demands a roll.
Pair.jump: Converge several choice branches back into one path with a Jump.

check.Summary: Asks the triggering player for a native dnd5e roll (skill, save, ability, tool) against a DC; branches on success/failure.
check.Usage: Pick the roll kind and key (e.g. Perception) and set the DC. The roll happens on the trigger player's client through the real dnd5e dialog - advantage, bonuses and features all apply; the chat card is suppressed and only the total comes back. Multiple checks can be combined with AND/OR. Success and failure pins lead to separate branches.
check.Tip1: Cancelling the roll dialog does not fail the check - the node re-arms and waits.
check.Tip2: The trigger actor makes the roll: make sure the flow starts with the right token (a null actor is the usual cause of weird outcomes).
check.Tip3: Hide the breakdown for secret DCs; show it for teaching moments.

Pair.choice: Offer the check as one option among safer paths.
Pair.condition: Gate the check itself - e.g. only rogues even get to try.
Pair.display: Narrate both outcomes with a Display beat on each branch.

condition.Summary: Silently routes the flow TRUE/FALSE based on actor facts - class, items, attributes. No player interaction.
condition.Usage:
Choose the target (usually the trigger actor) and add condition rows; combine with AND/OR. The runner evaluates instantly and fires exactly one of the true/false pins. With no rows configured the node passes (true).

[!tip] If the TRUE or FALSE branch looks wrong, check the trigger actor first - a null or unexpected actor is the most common cause, not a broken rule.
condition.Tip1: An unexpected FALSE is almost always the wrong trigger actor, not a broken comparison - check who started the flow first.
condition.Tip2: Chain two Condition nodes for mixed AND/OR logic instead of one giant rule.
condition.Tip3: Conditions read live actor data at run time - mid-session changes count.

Pair.check: Condition gates by fact; Check gates by roll - combine for 'only wizards may attempt this'.
Pair.choice: Branch after a choice to react differently per class or item.
Pair.jump: Send both branches to shared scenes with Jumps instead of duplicating nodes.

start.Summary: The entry marker of a graph - the run begins here. Purely a pass-through at runtime.
start.Usage: Place one START and wire it to your first beat. Flows are started from outside: the region behavior (token enters a zone), the generated macro, the Deck, or api.startFlow(pageUuid). The run's trigger actor - who rolls checks and is tested by conditions - is set by whoever/whatever started the flow.
start.Tip1: There is no live demo for START - it cannot trigger itself. Use 'Run from here' on any node in the editor instead.
start.Tip2: If meta.entry is unset the runner falls back to the first trigger-category node - keep exactly one START to stay predictable.
start.Tip3: A GM starting a flow with a player's token selected hands that player the controls.

Pair.display: The classic opener: START into a Display beat.
Pair.condition: Branch immediately on who triggered the flow.

region.Summary: Fires when a token moves into a scene Region with the StoryFlow behavior attached - the mover becomes the run's trigger actor.
region.Usage: Attach it in Scene Controls → Regions: create or select a Region, open its Behaviors tab, add a StoryFlow Trigger behavior, and drop this page onto it (optionally set the behavior's node field to a specific trigger.region node id if the graph has more than one - otherwise the run starts at the graph's entry node). Region events fire on EVERY connected client, but only the client that actually moved the token dispatches the run, and that token's actor becomes the trigger actor. The active GM client is the one that consumes once (disabling the behavior), since only it holds permission to edit it.
region.Tip1: whoTriggers/specificActorIds are defined on this payload but the region behavior does not filter by them yet - every token that enters fires the flow; gate by actor with a Condition node right after.
region.Tip2: Two Regions in one scene can drive two different flows from the same graph page by pointing each behavior's node field at a different trigger.region node id.
region.Tip3: once is consumed by the active GM only - with no GM online, a once-region never disables itself.

Pair.condition: Gate immediately on WHO stepped into the region - trigger actor's class, items, or attributes.
Pair.display: The classic ambush opener: a Region trigger straight into a Display beat.
Pair.notification: A quick toast ("You feel watched...") without stopping the scene for a full dialogue beat.

macro.Summary: Fires when a GM (or an external trigger like Monk's Active Tile Triggers) runs the macro generated for this node.
macro.Usage:
In the canvas app, use Generate Macro on a trigger.macro node to produce a script-macro command, then paste it into a hotbar slot. The macro resolves an acting actor by precedence - Monk's Active Tile Trigger entering token(s), else a selected token, else the running user's assigned character, else null - then calls api.startFlow(pageUuid, {nodeId, actorId}). Because actor resolution happens at RUN time from whatever is selected or entering, the same pasted macro works both for a GM manually firing it and for an automated tile trigger.

[!warning] After changing this node you must re-generate the macro and re-paste it into the hotbar - an already-pasted macro does not self-update.
macro.Tip1: The macro is baked with this node's id and the page uuid at generation time - rename the node or point at a different one, and you must re-generate and re-paste; editing the payload alone doesn't update an already-pasted macro.
macro.Tip2: If nothing is selected/entering and the running user has no assigned character, actorId is null - any downstream Condition targeting the trigger actor reads no actor and likely fails.
macro.Tip3: whoTriggers/specificActorIds exist on the payload but the generated macro doesn't filter by them - it always starts the flow when run; add a Condition node to gate.

Pair.condition: Guard on the macro's resolved actor before letting the scene continue.
Pair.branch: Let the GM who ran the macro pick the outcome by hand - no player roll involved.
Pair.display: Fire the macro to kick off a GM-cued cutscene.

weather.Summary: Fires when the ACTIVE scene's weather effect is set to the configured key.
weather.Usage: Pick a weather key from the dropdown (populated from the scene's available weather effects). The trigger listens on Foundry's updateScene hook and only reacts when the update actually touches the weather field on the currently-active scene. There is no trigger actor - the active GM client evaluates and drives the run, so downstream Condition nodes checking target:"trigger" find no actor.
weather.Tip1: Only the ACTIVE scene counts - changing weather on a scene nobody is viewing never fires, even with a matching key.
weather.Tip2: The match only checks that the weather field was touched and equals the payload's key - re-applying the SAME weather (e.g. a Simple Weather reroll of an unchanged forecast) refires it too, unless you set once.
weather.Tip3: actorId is always null here - pair Condition on something other than the trigger actor, or skip actor logic entirely.

Pair.display: Open with a mood beat the moment the storm rolls in.

action.light: Dim or flicker scene lighting to match the new weather.

Pair.notification: A quiet toast ("The rain begins...") without pulling players into a dialogue.

time.Summary: Fires once when the world clock crosses into a new time-of-day phase (dawn/day/dusk/night) that matches the configured phase.
time.Usage: Pick one of the four phases. The trigger listens on updateWorldTime, computes the current hour (via Simple Calendar if active, else worldTime/3600), and only fires on the actual TRANSITION into the chosen phase - not every tick while already inside it. There is no trigger actor; the active GM drives the run.
time.Tip1: It fires on the edge, not the level - jumping world time by many hours at once (e.g. a long rest) still fires this once per new phase entered, not once per hour.
time.Tip2: Phase boundaries are fixed: dawn 5-8, day 8-17, dusk 17-20, night 20-5 - not configurable per calendar.
time.Tip3: actorId is always null - pair Condition on a world fact, not the trigger actor.

Pair.display: Announce the time change with a short narration beat.
Pair.condition: Gate on a WORLD fact (e.g. a quest flag) since there's no trigger actor to check.

action.changeScene: Swap to a night-lit version of the map the moment dusk falls.

rest.Summary: Fires when an actor completes a short or long rest, filtered by rest type and who rested.
rest.Usage: Choose restType (any/short/long) and whoTriggers (any/party/specific actors). The trigger listens on dnd5e's restCompleted hook and reports the resting actor as the run's trigger actor, so downstream checks/conditions can react to THAT character specifically. party mode matches any actor with a player owner; specific matches only the listed actor ids.
rest.Tip1: The resting actor IS the trigger actor here (unlike weather/time) - Condition/Check nodes targeting the trigger see the resting character, not whichever client the GM runs.
rest.Tip2: restType reads the dnd5e result's long/short flag directly - verify live if a system update ever renames that result shape.
rest.Tip3: party mode only checks actor.hasPlayerOwner - an NPC ally with a player owner assigned still counts as party.

Pair.condition: Only continue if the resting actor is (or isn't) a specific class or state.
Pair.display: A quiet "you wake refreshed..." beat after the party rests.

action.healDamage: Top off HP beyond what the native rest already restored, e.g. a magic tent effect.

door.Summary: Fires when a wall/door changes to the configured state (open/closed/locked), scoped to a required Tagger tag.
door.Usage: Pick the target doorState, a Tagger tag (required to match - an untagged trigger never fires), and tagScope (active scene only, or all scenes). The trigger listens on updateWall, only reacting when the update actually touches the door state, and needs the Tagger module active to resolve tags. There is no trigger actor; the active GM drives the run.
door.Tip1: A tag is REQUIRED - the matcher demands a non-blank tag AND a tag match, so leaving it blank means the trigger can never fire, not "match any door".
door.Tip2: Needs the Tagger module active - without it, tags read as empty and the tag check always fails.
door.Tip3: actorId is always null - the door doesn't know who opened it; gate on world state, not the trigger actor.

action.door: Lock the door back behind the party right after the flow that unlocked it.

Pair.condition: Gate on a quest flag before letting the door event mean anything.
Pair.display: A creak-and-reveal beat the moment the tagged door opens.

timer.Summary: Fires on a repeating game-time interval anchored to a calendar date, independent of any world event.
timer.Usage: Set an anchor (year/month/day/hour) and an interval (every × unit: hours/days/weeks/months). The trigger listens on updateWorldTime and fires once per tick that crosses one or more grid boundaries - a big time jump (e.g. a long rest) still fires it exactly ONCE, not once per boundary skipped. once makes it single-shot; otherwise it re-arms forever on the fixed anchor+k·interval grid, tracked in persisted trigger state so a reload doesn't re-fire missed boundaries.
timer.Tip1: Months/weeks are fixed at 28-day months / 7-day weeks (the module's own calendar), not whatever a Simple Calendar custom calendar defines.
timer.Tip2: A disabled timer still silently advances its internal clock on every world-time tick, so re-enabling it later doesn't back-fire for every boundary it missed.
timer.Tip3: actorId is always null - this is a world clock, not tied to any character.

Pair.display: A recurring omen or countdown beat every N days.
Pair.condition: Gate a scheduled event on a quest flag before it fires for real.
Pair.notification: A subtle toast marking the passage of time without stopping play.

hp.Summary: Fires when a watched actor's HP crosses DOWNWARD through a threshold (percent, flat value, or death at 0 HP).
hp.Usage:
Choose mode (percent of max HP, flat value, stage boundary, or death at 0 HP or below) and threshold where applicable, plus whoTriggers/specificActorIds to scope which actors are watched. It listens on updateActor (linked and unlinked tokens alike), comparing the HP just before vs. just after the update, and fires ONLY on the downward crossing - old HP above the limit, new HP at or below it, so dropping HP exactly TO the threshold fires - and it re-arms itself once the actor heals back above the line. maxFires (0 = unlimited) caps how many times one node can fire, tracked in persisted trigger state.

[!info] This pairs well with the Boss Bar plugin action node, and setting this trigger to stage mode fires it once per HP stage instead of once at a single threshold.
hp.Tip1: It's edge-triggered, not level-triggered - an actor already sitting below the threshold when the flow is authored won't refire until they heal above it and drop below again.
hp.Tip2: The actor whose HP dropped IS the trigger actor - Condition/Check nodes after it see that character.
hp.Tip3: maxFires counts per NODE, not per actor - with whoTriggers:"party" one unlucky character bleeding out repeatedly can burn through the whole cap for everyone.

Pair.condition: Only escalate ("bloodied" narration) if the dropping actor is the party's tank, say.

action.healDamage: A guardian-angel effect: heal the actor back the instant they cross the threshold.

Pair.display: A "you're badly wounded" beat the moment HP crosses the line.

spell.Summary: Fires when a watched actor casts one of the listed spells (or ANY spell, if the list is empty).
spell.Usage: Add spell rows by dragging spell items into the list (matched by source uuid/name, tolerant of world vs. compendium copies), and set whoTriggers/specificActorIds to scope which casters count. It listens on dnd5e's activity-use hook, only matching spell-type items owned by an actor; an empty spell list matches ANY spell cast by a scoped actor. The casting actor is the run's trigger actor.
spell.Tip1: An empty spell list is NOT "never fires" - it means "match any spell"; combine with whoTriggers:"specific" if you only want to watch one caster's spellbook.
spell.Tip2: Matching is by item identity (uuid/sourceId/name), not by spell school or level - "watch for Fireball" won't catch a reskinned copy with a different name.
spell.Tip3: Fires once per activity use - verify live that a multi-target or upcast doesn't fire it more than once on your dnd5e version.

Pair.condition: Only react if the caster is a specific class or has a specific item.
Pair.display: A "the air crackles with magic" beat the instant the watched spell lands.
Pair.check: Follow up with a save/check of your own reacting to the cast, e.g. a ward the spell just triggered.

roll.Summary: Fires when a watched actor's save, ability check, skill check, attack roll, or applied status effect matches one of the node's rules.
roll.Usage: Add rule rows (kind: save/ability/skill/attack/effect; optional detail like a specific skill key; optional outcome: any/success/failure/critical/fumble), scoped by whoTriggers/specificActorIds. Rules are OR'd together - any one matching rule fires the node; an empty rule list never fires. It listens on dnd5e's roll hooks (and createActiveEffect for the effect kind) and reports the roller/affected actor as the run's trigger actor; success/failure needs a known DC/AC on the roll, else it reads as unknown and only any/critical/fumble outcomes can still match.
roll.Tip1: Effect rules ignore outcome entirely (always normalized to "any") - they match purely on the status id in detail.
roll.Tip2: A roll with no target DC/AC (e.g. a bare ability check with no set target) has an unknown success - rules asking for success/failure never match it, only any/critical/fumble can.
roll.Tip3: Rules OR together by design (no AND/NONE) - to require BOTH a specific roll AND a specific actor, that's what whoTriggers is for; you can't AND two roll kinds on one node.

Pair.condition: Only react to the roll if the roller is a specific class or holds a specific item.
Pair.display: A dramatic beat the instant a critical hit or fumble lands.
Pair.check: Chain a follow-up check that reacts to the roll that was just detected.

combat.Summary: Fires when a combat encounter starts, ends, or reaches a specific round.
combat.Usage: Pick the event: start (initiative begins), end (the encounter is deleted/closed), or roundChange with a round number (0 = every round, N = only when round N begins). Like all event triggers it registers on every client and self-gates to the active GM, who starts the flow; use once for one-shot cinematics and enabled as a kill switch. There is no live demo - start or advance a real combat to see it fire.
combat.Tip1: roundChange with round 0 fires on EVERY new round - great for recurring hazards, dangerous with once unchecked on anything loud.
combat.Tip2: Combat events have no single acting player, so the run's trigger actor comes from the GM-side start - gate per-actor logic with a Condition inside the flow instead.

Pair.display: An opening beat the moment initiative is rolled sells the ambush.
Pair.condition: Branch the combat-start flow on who is actually in the fight.
Pair.transition: A cinematic wipe into round one makes the start of combat land.

levelup.Summary: Fires when a character gains a class level - the leveling character becomes the run's trigger actor.
levelup.Usage: Optionally set a level (0 = any level-up, N = only when the character reaches exactly level N) and who triggers: any actor, party (player-owned actors), or specific actors dragged into the list. The trigger watches the dnd5e class item's level increasing, so it fires however the level is granted - the level-up dialog, manual edit, or another module. Like all event triggers it registers on every client and self-gates to the active GM, who starts the flow; use once for one-shot milestones and enabled as a kill switch. There is no live demo - level a real character to see it fire.
levelup.Tip1: The leveling character IS the trigger actor, so Condition nodes targeting the trigger and Check rolls address them directly - no extra gating needed.
levelup.Tip2: A multi-level jump (e.g. 4 → 6 in one edit) fires once with the final level - an exact-level node set to the skipped level (5) does not fire.

Pair.display: A congratulatory beat the moment the level lands makes milestones feel earned.
Pair.notification: A light toast ("Mira reaches level 5!") announces the milestone without stopping play.

action.giveItem: Grant a milestone reward - a feat scroll, a signature weapon - the moment the level is reached.

notification.Summary: Fire-and-forget on-screen notification: toast, epic item reveal, or secret unveil.
notification.Usage: Pick a style and write the text. Toast is a corner notification; epic and secret present a drag-dropped item cinematically. The flow advances immediately - the notification does not wait to be dismissed.
notification.Tip1: Epic/secret need an item reference - drag one onto the field in the inspector.
notification.Tip2: For text the players must read before continuing, use a Display beat instead.

Pair.display: Follow a secret reveal with a Display beat explaining what they found.
Pair.audio: A sting right before an epic reveal sells the moment.

text.Summary: Narrator prose: typewriter body text with no speaker name or portrait.
text.Usage: Write the body text; unlike Display there is no speaker name or portrait, only the words. Background can stay transparent (the live scene shows through) or carry the previous node's backdrop. The same pacing controls apply: typewriter speed, or auto-advance with a delay instead of a click. One input, one output.
text.Tip1: Use Text for narration and scene-setting; switch to Display the moment a character is speaking.
text.Tip2: background: "carry" keeps whatever image the last beat set - mix Text and Display freely in one scene without flicker.
text.Tip3: autoAdvance turns this into a cutscene beat - no Continue button, it moves on by itself after the delay.

Pair.display: Alternate Text (narration) with Display (dialogue) to build a scene.
Pair.wait: Follow a Text beat with a Wait for a dramatic pause before the next line.
Pair.choice: Close a run of Text beats with a Choice to hand control back to the player.

jump.Summary: Redirects the run to any other node in this graph by id - no output pin, the path just teleports.
jump.Usage: Pick a target node from the graph (the field lists every node in the current graph). At runtime the run continues there directly, skipping edges entirely. Jump has no output pin - wiring after a Jump is pointless, the redirect already happened. Great for converging several branches back onto one shared beat instead of duplicating it.
jump.Tip1: showLink draws a dashed authoring line from the Jump to its target on the canvas - leave it on so the wiring stays readable.
jump.Tip2: A blank targetNodeId just ends the path here - Jump degrades safely if you forget to wire it.
jump.Tip3: Jump ignores its own position in the fan-out graph - it can point backwards (a loop) or forwards; the runner doesn't care which.

Pair.display: Converge multiple Display chains onto one Jump target instead of repeating the ending.
Pair.choice: Send two or more Choice branches to the same Jump so they share a common continuation.
Pair.condition: Route both a Condition's true and false paths to distinct beats that Jump back to the same place.

wait.Summary: Pauses the run for a fixed number of seconds, then continues - no player interaction.
wait.Usage: Set seconds (0-120). The run holds there and advances automatically once the time elapses; nothing is shown to players by default, so pair it with a Display/Text/Notification if the pause needs a reason on screen. One input, one output.
wait.Tip1: A Wait with seconds: 0 is a legal no-op - handy as a placeholder while you're still wiring a graph.
wait.Tip2: Long waits (music stings, environmental beats) read better paired with a Transition or ambient audio than silence.

Pair.display: Wait between two Display beats for a beat of silence instead of an instant cut.
Pair.text: A Wait after narration gives the moment room to land before the next line.
Pair.transition: Hold on a faded screen with Wait, then use Transition to reveal the next scene.

branch.Summary: GM path selector: the GM (or the trigger player) picks one of several configured output paths at play time.
branch.Usage: Add paths - each becomes a positional output pin (path_0, path_1, …). Set decider to "gm" (the active GM chooses) or "trigger" (the triggering player chooses). Unlike Choice, this prompts a single decider rather than offering options to everyone; use it for GM-authored pacing decisions rather than player agency.
branch.Tip1: decider: "gm" prompts you, the GM, mid-run - expect that prompt when testing a graph with a Branch node.
branch.Tip2: Reordering or deleting paths remaps the positional pins the same way Choice does - recheck wiring after edits.
branch.Tip3: Branch is deterministic (someone picks); reach for Random instead when you want the story to vary on its own.

Pair.choice: Use Choice for player agency, Branch for a GM's own storytelling fork in the same graph.
Pair.condition: Gate a Branch path so a choice is only offered when a Condition already allows it.
Pair.random: Combine a Branch (GM picks the theme) with a Random node inside one branch (who shows up).

random.Summary: Weighted-RNG path selector: the runner draws one of several configured output paths at play time.
random.Usage: Add paths, each with a weight - the runner draws one at random in proportion to its weight (equal weights = equal odds). Output pins are positional (rand_0, rand_1, …), same shape as Branch, but nobody is prompted; the pick happens instantly and silently.
random.Tip1: Weights are relative, not percentages - {70, 30} and {7, 3} draw identically; use whatever numbers read clearly to you.
random.Tip2: A path with weight 0 can still be wired and will simply never fire - useful for staging an option before you're ready to enable it.
random.Tip3: Random has no dedicated shape validator - a malformed row degrades gracefully in the weighted draw rather than erroring.

Pair.branch: Reach for Branch instead when the outcome should be a deliberate GM/player pick, not chance.
Pair.choice: Randomize flavor (which merchant, which ambient line) behind a Choice the player actually made.
Pair.condition: Gate which Random roll even runs, so luck only applies once prerequisites are met.

preload.Summary: Barrier node: waits for every connected client to finish fetching this graph's images/audio before the run continues.
preload.Usage: Place a Preload before an asset-heavy beat (a big reveal, a scene change) so every player's client has the files cached before it plays. confirmBeforeRun adds a GM confirmation prompt once the barrier is satisfied - off means it releases automatically the instant loading finishes. One output pin only; there is no failure branch.
preload.Tip1: In a solo-GM test world the barrier is satisfied instantly (only one participant) - the real payoff shows with a full table on a slow connection.
preload.Tip2: confirmBeforeRun: true is a good safety valve before something destructive/irreversible (a scene change); turn it off for routine pacing.

action.changeScene: Preload the destination scene's assets, then Change Scene - no pop-in on arrival.

Pair.display: Preload lets the very next Display's backdrop/portrait appear instantly instead of loading in.
Pair.wait: A short Wait after a non-confirming Preload gives a beat to settle even when loading was already instant.

end.Summary: Terminates one path through the graph. The run itself ends only once every path has settled.
end.Usage: Wire every dangling branch to an End node (or a Jump that eventually reaches one) - a graph is not required to have exactly one End; fan-out edges can each carry their own. The run as a whole finishes on a settle basis: once no path is still pending (every branch has reached an End, an unresolved wait, or simply stopped), the overlay closes for everyone.
end.Tip1: Multiple simultaneous End nodes are normal for a fan-out graph - you don't need to funnel every branch back to one.
end.Tip2: A node type the runner doesn't recognize still advances its "out" pin and loads as a gray placeholder - it is never silently dropped, so a stray dead end usually means a missing End, not a corrupted graph.

Pair.display: Close out a scene with a final Display beat right before the End.
Pair.jump: A Jump with a blank target behaves like an implicit End - prefer an explicit End node for clarity.

comment.Summary: A sticky-note annotation on the canvas - no pins, never part of the run.
comment.Usage: Drop a Comment anywhere to leave yourself (or a co-author) a note: why a branch exists, a TODO, a reminder about a dependency. It has no input or output pins, so no edge can ever reach it and the runner can never execute it - it is purely a canvas annotation, resizable like a sticky note.
comment.Tip1: Because nothing can wire to a Comment, there is nothing to test-run - the Node Guide's demo button is a no-op for this type by design.
comment.Tip2: Use Comments to mark WIP sections of a big graph before you fill them in - they're invisible to players and to the runner alike.

Pair.jump: Note the intent behind a Jump's target right next to it - the destination isn't always obvious from the canvas.
Pair.condition: Document a Condition's real-world intent ("only rogues") since its rows alone can be terse.

showImage.Summary: Shows a full-bleed image for a fixed duration, then advances - a poster/illustration beat.
showImage.Usage: Pick an image file and set seconds; the image displays full-screen and the run advances automatically once the timer elapses. There is no click-to-advance - treat it like a timed cutscene panel rather than a beat players linger on. One input, one output.
showImage.Tip1: seconds: 0 shows the image for a single frame before advancing - effectively unusable; give it at least a couple of seconds.
showImage.Tip2: Pair with a Transition for a fade in/out instead of a hard cut to and from the image.

Pair.display: Follow a Show Image with a Display beat to caption or react to what was just shown.
Pair.wait: Insert a Wait beforehand to build anticipation before the image reveals.
Pair.transition: Wrap the Show Image in fade Transitions so it doesn't pop in and out abruptly.

giveItem.Summary: Copies a dropped item onto the trigger actor, or removes a matching one from their inventory.
giveItem.Usage: Drag an item onto itemUuid and set quantity. mode "give" copies the item onto the RUN'S trigger actor (the world/compendium source is untouched); mode "remove" matches the actor's owned items by source uuid, id, or name and deletes whole stacks first, decrementing the final partial stack down to quantity. A missing/no trigger actor skips with a console warning - the flow still advances.
giveItem.Tip1: This always targets the trigger actor - there is no selected/all option here, unlike Heal/Damage or Give Gold.
giveItem.Tip2: remove matches by source/uuid/id/name, so it still finds a world-copy of a compendium item - but a renamed custom item may not match; verify live if names diverge.
giveItem.Tip3: No trigger actor (a null actorId) means this silently skips - same root cause as most "nothing happened" reports elsewhere in the graph.

Pair.condition: Gate the reward on a Condition (class, prior item) before handing it out.
Pair.notification: Follow up with a Notification (epic/secret style) to cinematically reveal what was just given.

action.giveGold: Pair an item reward with a gold reward for a quest payout beat.

healDamage.Summary: Rolls a formula once and applies it as damage or healing to the trigger actor, selected actors, or the whole party.
healDamage.Usage: Pick mode (damage/heal), a dice formula, and target: "trigger" (the run's actor), "selected" (the GM is prompted with a checklist dialog - the run PAUSES until they confirm), or "all" (every non-GM user's assigned character, falling back to every character actor if nobody's assigned). The roll applies once via dnd5e's native applyDamage (so resistances/temp HP work), then posts a chat card with the total.
healDamage.Tip1: target "selected" pauses the whole run at a GM dialog - don't use it inside a timed sequence you expect to run unattended.
healDamage.Tip2: "all" is the party's ASSIGNED characters, not everyone currently online - an unassigned player's actor won't be touched even if they're logged in.
healDamage.Tip3: One roll is shared across every resolved target (same damage/heal amount for all), not a separate roll per actor.

trigger.hp: Follow an HP-threshold trigger with Heal/Damage for a guardian-angel or bleed-out effect.

Pair.condition: Gate who takes the damage/heal with a Condition first (e.g. only if poisoned).
Pair.check: Apply damage only down the failure branch of a Check.

giveGold.Summary: Rolls a formula once and adds (or subtracts) that many gp to the trigger actor, selected actors, or the whole party.
giveGold.Usage: Pick mode (give/take) and a dice/flat formula; target works exactly like Heal/Damage ("trigger"/"selected" with a pausing GM dialog/"all" the party). The roll is applied to each resolved actor's system.currency.gp directly, then a chat card announces the total.
giveGold.Tip1: There is no canned demo for this node: even a blank-default payload (10 gp to the trigger actor) validates fine but genuinely writes to a character's purse - always test it against a throwaway actor first.
giveGold.Tip2: mode "take" clamps at 0 gp - you can't drive an actor's gold negative by overtaking.
giveGold.Tip3: target "selected" pauses the run at a GM checklist dialog, same as Heal/Damage - plan for that pause in a timed graph.

Pair.trader: Reward gold right before opening a Trader so players can immediately spend it.
Pair.condition: Only pay out if a Condition (quest flag, class) says the reward is earned.
Pair.notification: A toast ("+50 gp") reinforces the chat card without forcing a read.

applyEffect.Summary: Applies or removes a standard status effect (CONFIG.statusEffects, e.g. blinded, prone) on the trigger, selected, or all actors.
applyEffect.Usage: Pick the effect from the runtime dropdown and mode (apply/remove); targeting matches Heal/Damage/Give Gold exactly ("selected" pauses on a GM checklist dialog). Each resolved actor gets actor.toggleStatusEffect(effectId, {active}) called directly - the effect's own duration/end conditions (if any) are whatever that status normally carries in your dnd5e build.
applyEffect.Tip1: effectId must be picked from the dropdown - it can't be typed, and a blank selection fails validation entirely.
applyEffect.Tip2: toggleStatusEffect is idempotent per actor - reapplying the same effect with mode "apply" doesn't stack a second copy.
applyEffect.Tip3: target "selected" pauses the run at a GM dialog just like Heal/Damage and Give Gold - the same targeting code is shared underneath.

Pair.condition: Gate which actors are even eligible before applying a status.
Pair.check: Apply a status only down a Check's failure branch (e.g. failed save → poisoned).

trigger.roll: React to a detected roll/effect trigger by applying a matching status of your own.

changeScene.Summary: Activates a scene for the whole table, or just previews it on the GM's own client.
changeScene.Usage: Drag a Scene onto sceneId. activate: true calls scene.activate() - every connected client is switched to that scene, same as clicking Activate in the Scenes sidebar. activate: false calls scene.view() instead - a GM-only preview that does not move players. A missing scene warns and skips; the flow still advances.
changeScene.Tip1: activate: true moves EVERY player's view immediately - don't fire it mid-conversation unless you mean to relocate the whole table.
changeScene.Tip2: activate: false is handy for a GM to eyeball a destination scene mid-run without disrupting what players currently see.
changeScene.Tip3: Pair with Preload Scene beforehand so the new scene's assets are already cached - activate doesn't wait for anything to load.

action.preloadScene: Preload the destination's assets before activating it, so there's no pop-in.

trigger.time: Swap to a night map the moment a Time trigger crosses into dusk.

Pair.display: Narrate the transition with a Display beat right before (or after) the scene change.

preloadScene.Summary: Tells clients to fetch a scene's images/audio into cache ahead of time, without switching to it.
preloadScene.Usage: Drag a Scene onto sceneId. allClients: true asks every connected client to preload (not just the GM), so a later Change Scene is instant for everyone. This is fire-and-forget - the node doesn't wait for the preload to finish before advancing (unlike the general-purpose Preload barrier node, which does).
preloadScene.Tip1: Unlike the Preload node, this one does NOT block the run waiting for assets to finish loading - it just kicks off the fetch and moves on.
preloadScene.Tip2: allClients: false only preloads on the GM's own client - usually not what you want before a real scene change for the table.

action.changeScene: The classic pairing: Preload Scene now, Change Scene later, no pop-in on arrival.

Pair.preload: Use the general Preload barrier instead when the run should actually WAIT for loading to finish.

token.Summary: Moves, spawns, or deletes tokens on a scene.
token.Usage: Pick operation (move/create/delete). move/delete resolve tokens from a captured selection (the "Capture Selected Tokens" inspector button), a Tagger tag, or one or more dropped Actors (any token of those actors currently on the active scene - survives token re-placement); create spawns a dropped Actor's prototype token instead. All three need a destination for move/create: a captured point, a captured tile's CURRENT center (re-resolved live, so a moved/resized tile still lands correctly), or a Tagger-tagged marker. move is same-scene only - a resolved token whose scene doesn't match the destination scene is skipped with a warning, never teleported cross-scene.
token.Tip1: A captured destination tile is stored by id, not baked coordinates - move the tile later in the editor and this node still lands on its new center.
token.Tip2: move never crosses scenes - if your captured tokens and destination are on different scenes, that group is skipped with a console warning, not an error.
token.Tip3: Tag mode needs the Tagger module active for both source AND destination tags; without it, tag-based targeting/destinations resolve to nothing (fail-soft, not a crash).

action.door: Move a token through a doorway right after Action: Door opens it.

trigger.region: Spawn a reinforcement token the moment a Region trigger fires.

Pair.condition: Only relocate/delete tokens that pass a Condition check first.

macro.Summary: Runs a referenced Foundry Macro and/or a block of inline code on the GM-authority client, with the run's actor/token in scope.
macro.Usage: Drag a Macro onto macroUuid and/or write inline code (both can be used together; both are optional - a fully blank payload is a legal no-op). The code runs as an async function with (actor, token, speaker, scope) in scope, where actor/token/speaker resolve from the run's trigger actor. It executes ONLY on the active-GM client - the same trust model as running any other Foundry script macro.
macro.Tip1: This has the same trust level as any GM-authored script macro - inline code has full API access; only put graphs you trust in front of players who can edit them.
macro.Tip2: A thrown error in the macro or the inline code is caught and logged to console, but does NOT fail the node - the flow still advances past it.
macro.Tip3: actor/token are null when the run has no trigger actor (e.g. a world-event trigger like weather/time) - code that assumes a real actor should guard for null.

trigger.macro: The generated macro from a trigger.macro node calls api.startFlow - chain a second Action: Macro deeper in the same graph for a scripted follow-up.

Pair.condition: Gate whether the macro even runs behind a Condition.
Pair.branch: Let the GM choose a path, then run different macros per branch.

door.Summary: Opens, closes, locks, toggles, or converts (wall/door/secret) the targeted walls.
door.Usage:
Pick operation and targeting: "captured" uses walls selected via the "Capture Selected Walls" inspector button (baked to specific wall ids on a specific scene); "tag" resolves walls tagged with a Tagger tag at RUN time (requires the Tagger module active). Writes go through Scene#updateEmbeddedDocuments so every client sees the change instantly, natively - no socket message needed.

[!tip] Tag targeting needs the Tagger module active; StoryFlow warns and does nothing if Tagger is not installed or enabled, it never assumes the tags exist.
door.Tip1: Captured mode bakes specific wall ids at authoring time - if you later delete/replace those walls, the node silently has nothing to act on (capture again).
door.Tip2: Tag mode needs the Tagger module active; without it (or with no matching tag), it warns and skips rather than erroring - safe, but silent if you forget to check the console.
door.Tip3: makeDoor/makeSecret/makeWall convert a plain wall segment into a door type - handy for a secret passage that only appears mid-story.

trigger.door: Pair with a Door trigger to react when the SAME tagged door later changes state again.

action.light: Light up a newly-opened secret passage the moment the door node runs.

Pair.condition: Only unlock a door once a Condition (quest state, key item) passes.

light.Summary: Turns lights on/off/toggle, or partially reconfigures their properties (color, radius, animation, darkness range).
light.Usage:
Pick operation and targeting exactly like Action: Door (captured selection or a Tagger tag). configure mode is a PARTIAL update - every field defaults to "unchanged"/null and only fields you explicitly enable (setColor + the nullable numeric fields) get written; everything else on the light keeps its current value.

[!tip] Tag targeting needs the Tagger module active; StoryFlow warns and does nothing if Tagger is not installed or enabled, it never assumes the tags exist.
light.Tip1: configure only writes fields you've explicitly touched - leaving a field at its null/"unchanged" default leaves that property alone on the real light, it does not reset it to a default.
light.Tip2: Tag mode needs the Tagger module active; missing it (or no match) warns and skips - the flow still advances, nothing breaks.
light.Tip3: on/off/toggle just flip hidden - full configure control (color, animation, darkness range) is a separate operation, not layered on top.

trigger.weather: Dim or flicker lighting the instant a matching Weather trigger fires.

action.door: Kill the torches the moment a secret door opens, for atmosphere.
action.effect: Layer a Sequencer glow effect on top of a light that just turned on.

effect.Summary: Plays a Sequencer/JB2A visual effect at a token, a captured point, a captured line, the screen, or a set of tokens.
effect.Usage:
Type or pick a Sequencer database path (animation) and a target mode. Persistent effects (persist: true) need a name and stay until an End Effect node (or Sequencer's own Effect Manager) ends them; non-persistent ones with waitUntilFinished hold the run until playback completes. Requires the Sequencer module (and usually a JB2A pack) active - without it, this warns and advances immediately, never blocking the run.

[!warning] This requires the Sequencer module (with an animation database such as JB2A) to be active; without it the node fails soft and simply advances, no animation plays.
effect.Tip1: No Sequencer module active? The node fails soft: a console warning, a GM-facing notification, and the flow advances right past it - it never hangs a run.
effect.Tip2: persist: true effects MUST have a name - that name (and this graph's page uuid as an origin) is how an End Effect node later finds and ends exactly this effect, not someone else's Sequencer animation.
effect.Tip3: waitUntilFinished pauses the run until the animation completes - leave it off for pure atmosphere you don't want to gate pacing on.

action.endEffect: Persist an effect here, then clean it up later with an End Effect node.

Pair.check: Play an impact effect on the failure branch of a Check.
Pair.notification: Layer a quick Notification toast alongside a bigger visual effect.

endEffect.Summary: Ends persistent Sequencer effects this module created - by name, by source graph, or all of them; or deletes a whole mass-placed tile group.
endEffect.Usage: Pick mode: "name" ends one persistent effect by its label; "graph" ends every persistent effect this SAME graph page created (matched by page uuid origin); "all" ends every persistent effect ANY StoryFlow graph created (namespaced storyflow: - it never touches another module's Sequencer effects); "tiles" instead deletes every tile in an Action: Tiles placement group (plain scene document deletion, no Sequencer needed for that mode).
endEffect.Tip1: "all" only reaches effects this module namespaced (storyflow:) - it can never accidentally end a different module's or the GM's own manually-placed Sequencer effect.
endEffect.Tip2: "tiles" mode doesn't need the Sequencer module at all - it's a plain document delete on the scene's tiles in that group.
endEffect.Tip3: Ending an effect (or group) that isn't currently running is a safe no-op - this node is idempotent by design.

action.effect: The natural pair: persist an effect with Action: Effect, clean it up later with this node.
action.tiles: Delete a whole mass-placed tile group with mode "tiles" once its scene is done with.

tiles.Summary: Mass-places tagged, animated tiles (using a Sequencer file as the texture) across a scene, or shows/hides/toggles an already-placed group.
tiles.Usage:
Set animation (a Sequencer database path - its first playable file becomes the tile texture), a group name (stamped on every tile via a flag so they can be found again), size/rotation/opacity for placement, and operation (show/hide/toggle) for an already-placed group. Placement itself happens through the canvas app's Mass Place button, not this payload alone - the node's operation then toggles visibility on whatever's already in that group.

[!warning] This requires the Sequencer module (with an animation database such as JB2A) to be active; without it the node fails soft and simply advances, no tiles appear.
tiles.Tip1: The group name is how this node (and End Effect's "tiles" mode) finds its own tiles later - reusing a group name across unrelated placements will affect all of them together.
tiles.Tip2: Placed tiles are editable natively afterward (drag, resize, restyle in the Tiles layer) - this node's fields only apply at PLACEMENT time, not on every show/hide/toggle.
tiles.Tip3: Deleting a whole tile group is End Effect's job (mode "tiles"), not this node - this one only toggles visibility.

action.endEffect: Delete the whole placed group later with End Effect's tiles mode.
action.effect: Layer a one-shot Sequencer effect on top of a tile group that just appeared.

Pair.condition: Only reveal a hazard/decoration tile group once a Condition allows it.

bossBar.Summary: Shows or hides the cinematic Boss HP Bar on every client, tracking one actor's health live.
bossBar.Usage: Drag ANY one actor into the Actor field (or pick it from the list) and choose the operation: show raises the banner on all connected clients - name intro, blood-liquid bar, stage diamonds at 2/3 and 1/3, shield thread fed by temp HP - and hide lowers it. HP tracks the actor document itself, so damage and healing from any source move the bar instantly; reaching 0 HP plays the death sequence on its own. An optional Label overrides the displayed name.
bossBar.Tip1: One bar at a time - showing a new boss replaces the current one; wire a hide node (or use the Token HUD skull button) when the fight ends early.
bossBar.Tip2: The bar's stages are the same crossings the HP Trigger's Boss Stage mode fires on - pair them to script phase transitions without duplicating thresholds.

trigger.combat: Raise the banner the moment initiative is rolled with a Combat trigger.
trigger.hp: An HP Trigger in Boss Stage mode scripts each phase change of the same bar.

Pair.display: A Display beat introducing the boss lands harder with the banner rising behind it.

modifyReputation.Summary: Adjusts an actor's standing with a faction: add, subtract, or set the reputation value outright.
modifyReputation.Usage: Pick the faction, a mode (add/subtract/set) and an integer value, and the target - the trigger actor, the currently selected tokens, or all player characters. The write runs on the GM-authority client and the flow advances immediately. Reputation tiers then drive the rest of the module (trader prices, faction visibility, conditions).
modifyReputation.Tip1: The faction is a required pick - the dropdown lists your registered factions; with none configured the node is a warned no-op.
modifyReputation.Tip2: "set" overwrites unconditionally - prefer add/subtract for repeatable scenes so a re-run doesn't clobber earned standing.
modifyReputation.Tip3: target "trigger" follows the run's trigger actor - the usual suspect when reputation lands on the wrong character.

Pair.condition: Branch on the new standing right after the change with a Condition.
Pair.notification: Announce the reputation shift with a toast so the player knows why prices moved.
Pair.choice: Reward or punish a Choice branch with an immediate reputation swing.

modifyAffinity.Summary: Nudges one NPC's personal affinity toward the party: add, subtract, or set the approval value.
modifyAffinity.Usage: Paste the NPC actor's UUID (right-click the actor → Copy UUID), pick add/subtract/set and an integer value. The GM-authority client applies the change and the flow advances immediately. Affinity is per-NPC approval - the personal counterpart to faction-wide reputation.
modifyAffinity.Tip1: The actor UUID is required and plain text - a typo makes the node a warned no-op, so copy it from the document, don't type it.
modifyAffinity.Tip2: Like reputation, "set" clobbers - use add/subtract in repeatable dialogue so re-running a scene doesn't reset earned approval.

Pair.choice: The classic use: each dialogue Choice branch shifts the NPC's approval differently.
Pair.condition: Branch a later scene on the accumulated affinity with a Condition.
Pair.display: Let the NPC's Display line acknowledge the shift so players feel the needle move.

showOnMap.Summary: Pans the camera to a saved map location on every client, hiding the cinematic overlay for the duration.
showOnMap.Usage:
Use the "Confirm Camera Location" inspector button to capture a scene + pan target/scale (from the GM's own current camera), then set duration (how long the pan takes AND how long the map stays visible before the Out pin fires) and audience ("all" or "players" - the GM's own camera only moves for "all"). The overlay hides for EVERYONE regardless of audience so the GM watches the reveal too; it automatically re-shows on the next content beat (Display/Choice/Check) after this node.

[!tip] While the camera pans, the dialogue overlay hides on every client and returns automatically on the next beat - this is expected behavior, not a bug.
showOnMap.Tip1: This really moves every targeted client's camera - safe, but noticeable; don't fire it mid-conversation unless the reveal is the point.
showOnMap.Tip2: audience "players" still hides the GM's overlay, it just doesn't move the GM's own camera - the GM keeps their current view while players see the map.
showOnMap.Tip3: There's no live demo for this node: sceneId is a required captured reference, so it only runs meaningfully once you've clicked Confirm Camera Location in a real scene.

Pair.display: Follow the reveal with a Display beat once the camera lands, to narrate what's shown.
Pair.trader: Pan to the merchant's stall right before opening the Trader node.
Pair.notification: A quick toast right after the pan reinforces what just came into view.

trader.Summary: Opens a shop overlay backed by a Trader journal page - buy and sell tabs, reputation-aware pricing, and a stock ledger.
trader.Usage:
Drag a Trader page onto traderUuid. Buying draws down stock (and restocks over time per the trader's own restockDays setting); selling writes the sold goods back into the SAME catalog, so a player's sale can reappear as stock to buy. Faction-linked traders layer reputation multipliers/refusals and per-item rep-tier locks on top of catalog prices. Because the trader is a fan-out/settle node (like Choice), re-entering it via a loop-back edge rebuilds the shop state fresh from the trader page each time - restocked or newly-sold items show up correctly on re-entry, not a stale snapshot.

[!info] A buyer faction reputation can gate purchases entirely (refused at Hostile or Hated) and scales prices by tier; this is configured under the Factions system.
trader.Tip1: An empty trader (no items in its catalog) skips this node entirely - the Out pin fires immediately with no shop shown, not an error.
trader.Tip2: A faction with 'Refuse' reputation empties the whole Buy list for that player, even though the trader itself still has stock for everyone else.
trader.Tip3: Loop the trader's own continuation edge back to itself for a shop the player can keep browsing after each purchase - stock rebuilds live on every re-entry.

action.giveGold: Pay out gold right before opening the Trader so there's something to spend.

Pair.condition: Gate access to the whole shop behind a Condition (e.g. a quest flag or faction standing).
Pair.showOnMap: Pan to the merchant's location right before the shop opens.

journal.Summary: Opens a journal page for players, or writes/creates journal content as the GM-authority client.
journal.Usage: Pick operation: "open" broadcasts an open instruction so each client opens pageUuid locally if it matches target ("trigger"/"all"/"gm"); "write" appends or overwrites a TEXT page's content; "createPage" adds a new page to an existing JournalEntry; "createEntry" makes a brand-new JournalEntry (optionally in a folder), with an initial text page if content is set. Every write path runs ONLY on the active-GM client - Foundry then syncs the result to everyone natively.
journal.Tip1: "write" only works on a text-type page - pointing it at an image or PDF page silently skips with a console warning.
journal.Tip2: reveal only applies to createPage/createEntry - it grants OBSERVER ownership to the new document; leaving it off keeps the new page/entry GM-only.
journal.Tip3: The Node Guide has no canned demo for this node: open/write/createPage all need a real JournalEntryPage or JournalEntry reference, and createEntry writes a permanent new document into your world - none of that is safe to fire from a random world.

Pair.parchment: Follow an "open" journal read with a Parchment scroll for a more cinematic recap of the same lore.
Pair.condition: Only reveal a page once a Condition (quest state, a prior clue) says the players have earned it.
Pair.notification: A toast pointing at the newly-opened page reinforces that something worth reading just appeared.

parchment.Summary: Unfurls an aged-paper scroll/letter/book overlay showing either a referenced journal page or inline text, until the reader taps it closed.
parchment.Usage: Pick style (scroll/letter/book) and either drag a JournalEntryPage onto pageUuid or leave it blank and write text directly - a referenced page always wins over inline text when both are set. title/subtitle label the scroll's header, and audience ("all"/"players"/"trigger") decides who sees it; the run pauses until an eligible reader taps the parchment closed.
parchment.Tip1: A blank pageUuid falls back to the inline text field - you don't need a real Journal page to author a working Parchment beat.
parchment.Tip2: audience "trigger" shows the scroll ONLY to the triggering player, not the GM as well - the same rule as Notification's audience gate.
parchment.Tip3: The run is genuinely paused waiting for a tap - treat Parchment like Choice/Check, not something to chain inside a timed auto-advancing sequence.

Pair.journal: Reach for the Journal node instead when the content should live as a real, revisitable page in the sidebar.
Pair.display: Follow a Parchment reveal with a Display beat reacting to what was just read.
Pair.notification: A quick toast right before the scroll unfurls builds anticipation for the reveal.

audio.Summary: Plays an audio file once or on loop, broadcast to every client, with an optional persistent name for later control.
audio.Usage: Pick a file for audioPath (or drop a whole Playlist to populate tracks, picked randomly or sequentially each time this node fires) and mode (once/loop). volume can boost up to 150% for a quiet source. persistAfterEnd + name keep a looping track playing after this overlay closes, untouched by anything except a Stop Audio node targeting that same name (or "all").
audio.Tip1: A blank audioPath with no tracks list is a silent no-op - the node just advances, nothing plays.
audio.Tip2: persistAfterEnd only matters for a looping/ambient bed you want to survive past this node's own overlay - a one-shot sting never needs it.

Pair.display: Start a music bed just before a Display chain to score the scene.
Pair.transition: Time a sting to land right as a Transition's cover finishes sweeping in.
Pair.stopAudio: Every looping Audio node with persistAfterEnd needs a matching Stop Audio eventually, by its name.

stopAudio.Summary: Stops one named looping Audio track, or every StoryFlow-triggered sound at once.
stopAudio.Usage: Set mode to "name" and give the same name an Audio node used with persistAfterEnd, or mode "all" to stop everything this module currently has playing. It broadcasts a stop instruction to every client and advances immediately - there's nothing to wait for.
stopAudio.Tip1: mode "all" only reaches sounds THIS module started (namespaced) - it never touches another module's ambience or the GM's own Playlists.
stopAudio.Tip2: Stopping a name that isn't currently playing (or running "all" with nothing playing) is a safe no-op - nothing errors.

Pair.audio: The natural pair: loop an Audio node with persistAfterEnd, then Stop Audio by that same name later.
Pair.display: Cut the music right as a Display beat delivers the twist, for a hard emotional cut.

transition.Summary: Plays a full-screen cinematic wipe/fade over the overlay, masking the swap to whatever comes next.
transition.Usage:
Pick style (fade/iris/wipe/…), phase ("both" covers AND reveals in one node; "cover" sweeps in and holds, waiting for a later "reveal" node to clear it), color, duration, and an optional hold beat while fully covered. audience controls who plays it ("all"/"players"/"trigger"); direction only matters for wipe/blinds/curtain. The run advances to the next node HIDDEN under the cover, so nothing pops in - "both" reveals it immediately, "cover" leaves the mask up for a matching "reveal" node to clear later in the graph.

[!tip] Phase "both" covers the screen, swaps to the next beat while hidden, then reveals it - so the reveal always lands on the new content.
transition.Tip1: phase "both" is the simple case - one node, one seamless swap; reach for a "cover"+"reveal" pair only when something needs to happen in between while the screen is hidden.
transition.Tip2: hold only applies to phase "both" - it's the beat spent fully covered before the reveal starts, good for a hard scene cut.
transition.Tip3: direction is ignored entirely by fade/iris/dissolve/zoomBlur/ripple/shatter - it only steers wipe/blinds/curtain.

Pair.wait: Pair a "cover"-phase Transition with a Wait while something loads behind the mask, then a "reveal" node to clear it.
Pair.showImage: Wrap a Show Image beat in fade Transitions instead of a hard cut in and out.
Pair.display: Cut between two Display beats set in different places with a Transition instead of an instant jump.

screenAnimation.Summary: Plays a short one-shot camera/screen effect - shake, quick zoom, punch, tilt, or flash - then restores the view exactly.
screenAnimation.Usage:
Pick an Effect and its fields: Shake (intensity), Quick Zoom (direction in/out, amount), Camera Punch (direction, distance), Camera Tilt (direction, angle), or Screen Flash (color, opacity). Duration is in milliseconds. Target Users controls who sees it ("all" or just the "trigger" player). With Wait For Completion on, the next node runs only after the effect finishes; off, the flow continues immediately while it plays. The effect never permanently changes the canvas - zoom, pan, and rotation are always restored.

[!tip] Keep durations short (200-500 ms) - these are punchy accents for dramatic or comedic beats, not lasting camera moves.
screenAnimation.Tip1: Every effect is temporary and self-restoring - the camera's real zoom, position, and rotation are untouched, so it's safe to fire mid-scene.
screenAnimation.Tip2: Only one Screen Animation plays per client at a time - starting a new one cleanly cancels and restores any effect still running.
screenAnimation.Tip3: With Wait For Completion off, use it as a flourish that plays while the flow moves on; turn it on when the next beat should land only after the effect settles.

Pair.display: Fire a quick Shake or Flash right before a Display beat to punctuate a dramatic line.
Pair.transition: Use a Screen Flash as a sharp accent, or a full Transition when you need to actually mask a scene swap.
Pair.notification: Pair a Camera Punch with an epic Notification so the hit and the callout land together.

crate.Summary: A CS-style loot crate: each participating player spins a weighted item reel and keeps what they win.
crate.Usage: Add catalog rows (drag an item, set weight, optional glow color/style) plus title/text shown on the crate's lid, costGold per spin (0 = free), and maxSpins per player (0 = unlimited). Every online player with an assigned character can open the crate independently; the node's Out pin waits on a settle barrier - it doesn't fire until every participant has spun (or closed without spinning).
crate.Tip1: Each catalog row needs a real dropped Item - an empty catalog fails validation, so this node can't demo with placeholder data.
crate.Tip2: costGold is charged per spin from the spinning player's own purse; a player who can't afford it simply can't spin again until they have the gold.
crate.Tip3: maxSpins caps how many times each player personally can spin - it's a per-player limit, not a shared pool across the table.

action.giveGold: Pay out a little gold right before opening the crate so a costly spin feels earned.

Pair.trader: Let a crate's winnings feed straight into a Trader's stock, or be sold back for gold.
Pair.notification: Follow a big win with a Notification (epic style) for an extra cinematic beat.

cryptex.Summary: An interactive rotating-ring cryptex the players turn together live on screen to spell out a solution.
cryptex.Usage: Set rings (2-8) and alphabet (the glyphs each ring cycles through), then solution - one character per ring, each a letter present in alphabet. mode "auto" opens automatically the instant the rings match; mode "submit" adds a Try button, and a wrong attempt shakes the rings and (if maxAttempts > 0) decrements a shared attempt budget until it hits 0. The interactive player (plus the GM as a fallback) can turn the rings; success fires when solved, failure only when submit mode exhausts its attempts.
cryptex.Tip1: auto mode never fires failure at all - it has unlimited attempts by design, so only wire its failure pin if you plan to switch to submit mode later.
cryptex.Tip2: A blank solution validates fine (fail-open) but never actually solves - the cryptex just waits forever, so always fill it in before shipping a graph.
cryptex.Tip3: solution length must exactly match rings, and every character must appear in alphabet - a mismatch fails validation immediately in the editor.

Pair.check: Use Check for a dice-driven puzzle, Cryptex when you want the players to physically manipulate the solution instead.
Pair.condition: Gate whether the cryptex even appears behind a Condition (e.g. only after finding the matching journal clue).
Pair.display: Follow a solved cryptex with a Display beat narrating what opens or reveals.

quest.Summary: Drives the Quest Board from a flow: reveal quests or lore, flip statuses, reveal and complete objectives, or announce progress.
quest.Usage: Pick a target (a Quest or Lore page from your Quest Board) and an operation: revealQuest makes it visible to players, setStatus moves it between available/active/completed/failed, revealObjective and completeObjective work on one objective by id, announce pushes a progress banner, revealLore uncovers a lore page. The write runs on the GM-authority client and the flow advances immediately - no player interaction.
quest.Tip1: The target is a required reference - drag the quest or lore page in; a missing target makes the node a warned no-op at run time.
quest.Tip2: completeObjective does not auto-complete the quest - chain a second Quest node with setStatus when the last objective should close it.
quest.Tip3: Pair reveals with announce sparingly: every announce interrupts all players with a banner.

Pair.display: Narrate WHY the quest updated with a Display beat before the board changes.
Pair.notification: A toast is a lighter touch than the quest announce banner for minor progress.
Pair.condition: Gate objective completion on who actually did the deed with a Condition.

FieldHint.persistAfterEnd: Keeps this sound playing after the story ends, instead of cutting it off. It won't stop on its own - use a Stop Audio node targeting this sound's Name below (or set to stop "All") to end it later.
FieldHint.animationType: Which one-shot effect to play. Only the fields for the chosen effect are shown.
FieldHint.zoomAmount: How far to zoom, as a fraction of the current view (0.05-0.75).
FieldHint.distance: How far the camera punches, in pixels (5-200).
FieldHint.angle: How far to tilt, in degrees (1-45).
FieldHint.duration: Total effect length in milliseconds (50-3000). Hidden while audio sync is on - the audio drives all timing then (its length for Shake/Tilt; the stored value is each pulse's length for Quick Zoom, Camera Punch, and Screen Flash).
FieldHint.waitForCompletion: On: the next node runs only after the effect finishes. Off: the flow continues immediately.
FieldHint.synchronizeWithAudio: Shown only when the node directly before this one is an Audio node. On: each viewer's effect reacts to that same audio's loudness and peaks (footsteps shake, thunder flashes). With sync on, Shake and Tilt run for the audio's full length; Quick Zoom, Camera Punch, and Flash use Duration as the length of each reaction. Falls back to the ordinary one-shot when no Audio node precedes.
FieldHint.audioSensitivity: How readily the effect reacts to peaks (0-100). Lower ignores all but the strongest hits; higher reacts to subtler ones. 50 suits most clips.
